title.narrative: Business Environment Strengthening with Technology Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative:
The proposed program builds upon the government efforts to enhance and improve the business environment, leading to increased productivity, and competitiveness. This will, in turn, facilitate, and drive private sector development and investment, stimulating job creation. The program will reduce regulatory burden and increase transparency, facilitate investment overall but with a focus on strategically important sectors, and advance the transition to digital government. The program builds on earlier ADB support to enhance the business environment, including; i) the Increasing Competitiveness for Inclusive Growth Program, a which sought to generate employment by increasing competitiveness in the economy, ii) a series of financial sector development programs designed to increase the flow of credit to the private sector, iii) the Post-COVID-19 Business and Employment Recovery Program that sought create sustainable employment opportunities through support to existing and emerging businesses c, and iv) the Domestic Resource Mobilization Program, which was designed to create fiscal space to increase productive investments and promote more inclusive and sustainable growth. The program will also enable downstream investments in the renewable energy and information and communication technology (ICT) sectors by rationalizing the investment approval process.
The program is aligned with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028 and the 8-Point Socioeconomic Agenda which have identified regulatory transparency and efficiency as a priority. It also builds on the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act (Republic Act No. 11032) and will support implementation of Executive Order No. 18 (23 February 2023) which both seek to promote the Philippines as a top investment destination with a regulatory environment conducive to business operations. The program is also aligned with ADB's Country Partnership Strategy for the Philippines, 2024-2029, which includes boosting economic competitiveness as a key strategic pillar and fostering digital transformation and strengthening governance as cross-cutting themes. It will contribute to ADB's private sector development (PSD) shift by through pillar 4 of ADB's private sector development plan for the Philippines deepening digital enablement and ease of doing business and will adopt a whole-of-bank approach to addressing country-specific binding constraints to increase private sector contributions to economic growth and job creation. Finally, the program will contribute to ADB's Strategy 2030 and its midterm review. Following the Joint Multilateral Development Bank Methodological Approach for Assessment of Paris Agreement Alignment, the proposed operation has been assessed as aligned with the goals of the Paris Agreement.

Outcome: The average number of days taken to obtain the necessary pre-development permits and licenses reduced by 20% in at least three priority sectors aligned with the Strategic Investment Priority Plan. (2022 baseline: sectoral process mapping to establish number of days not completed)

description.narrative:
Action 1: To facilitate access to land for foreign investors, a bicameral committee of Congress approved the Investors' Lease Act that raises the allowable lease period for private lands to 99 years from 75 years, subject to certain conditions and requirements, and provides for the registration of lease contracts to secure lease-hold rights.
Action 2: To streamline the process for obtaining the necessary permits and licenses to start and operate a business, pursuant to Republic Act No. 11032 (RA11032),d ARTA conducted a phased rollout of the National Effort for the Harmonization of Efficient Measures of Inter-Related Agencies (NEHEMIA) by: 1.2.1 Completing end-to-end mapping of regulatory processes for the renewable energy and digital infrastructure sectors, two of the priorities identified in the Strategic Investment Priority Plan; and 1.2.2 Identifying regulatory process streamlining opportunities for these two sectors.
Action 3: To attract more investment by improving regulatory transparency and certainty for businesses, ARTA: 1.3.1 Launched the Philippine Business Regulations Information System (PBRIS) to provide a searchable digital database of regulations applicable to businesses across the full business life cycle; 1.3.2 Operationalized PBRIS by making available 100% of the executive orders, implementing rules and regulations, department orders and administrative orders identified during the end-to-end mapping of regulatory processes for the renewable energy and digital infrastructure sectors, two of the priorities identified in the Strategic Investment Priority Plan; and 1.3.3 Adopted a gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) Action Plan to ensure its public services are more gender-responsive and inclusive
Action 1: To provide investors with reliable information on land availability, DTI-BOI will strengthen its digital database of investment-ready locations by covering more economic zones and local government units (LGUs).
Action 2: To further streamline the process for obtaining the necessary permits and licenses to start and operate a business, ARTA will continue the phased rollout of NEHEMIA by: 2.2.1 Completing end-to-end mapping of regulatory processes for at least two more priority sectors aligned with the Strategic Investment Priority Plan; 2.2.2 Identifying regulatory process streamlining opportunities for at least these two additional sectors; and 2.2.3 Overseeing implementation of identified streamlining opportunities in at least three priority sectors.
Action 3: To further improve regulatory transparency and certainty for businesses, ARTA will: 2.3.1 Make available 100% of the executive orders, implementing rules and regulations, department orders and administrative orders identified during the end-to-end mapping of regulatory processes for at least two more priority sectors aligned with the Strategic Investment Priority Plan on PBRIS; 2.3.2 Enhance the functionality of PBRIS, including using artificial intelligence, to better meet investors' needs for identifying all relevant and in-effect regulations in the sector; 2.3.3 Issue formal guidance mandating all government agencies to make available through PBRIS all new regulations upon effectivity; and 2.3.4 Implement the GEDSI Action Plan to increase inclusiveness in its programs and activities.
